page.overview:
Who is Thomas Armitage?

Thomas "Elias" Armitage, commonly known as Tommy Bronny Armitage, is an original civilian character in Halloween: The Game. He is a 31-year-old single father living in Haddonfield, Illinois, who maintains the elaborate false identity of an eighteen-year-old high-school athlete. To most of the teenagers who know him, Tommy Bronny is simply another local jock: cocky, sociable, physically fit, and perpetually hanging around Haddonfield's younger crowd. In reality, Armitage is more than a decade older than the age he claims to be and has spent years constructing a second identity that allows him to blend into the town's teenage social scene. His secret becomes considerably more complicated because Thomas has a daughter, Beatrice Armitage, a troubled young woman who lives with him. Thomas keeps Beatrice largely out of public view, maintaining the appearance that he is simply another eighteen-year-old living a carefree life in Haddonfield. On the night of October 31, 1978, that carefully constructed life begins to unravel when Michael Myers returns to Haddonfield.

{| class="wikitable" ! Information ! Details Full name Thomas "Elias" Armitage - Nickname Tommy Bronny Armitage - Age 31 - Race African American - Gender Male - Height 6 ft 0 in - Weight 185 lbs (83 kg) - Status Deceased (Single Player)Determinable (Multiplayer) - Father Keith Armitage - Daughter Beatrice Armitage - Relationship Unknown - Sexuality Unknown

Thomas Armitage's childhood was far from stable. Growing up, he struggled with a distant and often difficult relationship with his mother, while his father, Keith Armitage, became the more dependable figure in his life. Keith ran a local furniture business, and Thomas spent much of his youth helping him with the work. Despite their hardships, the two remained close. Thomas struggled with growing up and never felt particularly comfortable with adulthood. He was drawn to the confidence and admiration that came with being young, athletic, and popular, eventually developing a habit of presenting himself as someone younger than he really was. After marrying Leshawna Armitage, Thomas briefly attempted to settle into a conventional adult life. Their marriage eventually ended in divorce, leaving Thomas as a single father to Beatrice Armitage. Rather than accepting the life he had built, Thomas retreated further into the identity he had created. He continued helping Keith with the family furniture business, but outside of work he became "Tommy Bronny"—an eighteen-year-old college football star who supposedly returned home every weekend to help his father. Thomas began presenting himself to local high-schoolers and the wider community as Tommy, carefully maintaining the illusion that he was still a teenager. What began as an escape from the disappointments of adulthood gradually became a permanent second identity.
